title: RegRadar Feature Registry
description: The Feature Registry maps product features to the code that implements them. RegRadar sends the entries that apply to a pull request's repository to the language model alongside the pull request diff, and the model rates each feature's regression risk. QA engineers maintain it through the Feature Registry page; see feature-registry.md.

repository.description: The GitHub repository the feature belongs to, as owner/name. When set, the entry is only used for pull requests from that repository. When null, the entry applies to pull requests from any repository. Stored in lower case.

feature_name.description: A feature an end user or tester would recognise, in plain language. Sent to the model as "feature", and must match the feature names used in the evaluation ground truth exactly.

code_areas.description: Class names, file names or directory names that implement the feature. These are compared with the files and functions changed in a pull request. At least one is required. Prefer names a QA engineer would genuinely know over an exhaustive list of internal classes.

endpoints.description: API routes the feature exposes. Optional, and usually empty for framework repositories.

description.description: One sentence describing what the feature covers. Sent to the model, so a clear description improves its reasoning about indirect dependencies.
examples: All form-based request validation using Laravel's validation layer

examples.description: Rule parsing and evaluation for form and request validation, including conditional rules
Handles user login, logout and token generation
